claim: The US Army carries out the planned controlled detonation of the degraded lead azide at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant near Middletown, Iowa, on Wednesday 25 November 2026 (Central time).

runs.reason:
**Base rate.** For an urgent military disposal operation with a publicly announced date two days away and no outstanding approvals, I’d start at about 75% for execution on that exact day. That’s a judgmental starting point, not a measured base rate; I didn’t find a reliable series of comparable cases.

**What moves this case.** The Army’s November 22 notice explicitly selected Wednesday, November 25, for better weather and time to put safeguards in place (**up**). The Justice Department’s November 21 filing warned that delay increased the risk of an uncontrolled explosion (**up**), but the Army had already moved the operation from November 20 to November 23 before selecting Wednesday (**down** for confidence in any exact date). ([army.mil](https://www.army.mil/article/296990/army_update_on_iowa_army_ammunition_plant))

The decisive update is November 23: AP reported that President Trump ordered the military to wait for both the Eighth Circuit’s clearance and Governor-elect Rob Sand’s agreement (**sharply down**). The court had stayed the EPA permit, and Sand had publicly questioned the rush to detonate. The Army’s earlier argument that it could proceed without the permit does not, by itself, remove the president’s hold. ([apnews.com](https://apnews.com/article/iowa-army-lead-detonation-trump-3844c3f93affd3ea9a91fa98199bc14a))

**Window risk.** I put a 92% chance on no qualifying detonation on November 25 Central time. The most likely way to miss the window is a delay beyond Wednesday, not permanent cancellation. Even if permission comes through, the Army still has to carry out at least the first detonation that day; an announcement or an accidental explosion would not count. ([army.mil](https://www.army.mil/article/296990/army_update_on_iowa_army_ammunition_plant))

Health agencies are already directing nearby residents to shelter on that day, and the current National Weather Service forecast for Middletown shows light winds, no daytime precipitation, and temperatures consistent with the conditions the Army cited when it selected the date.

Comparable last-minute military disposal operations that the service itself treats as an uncontrolled-explosion risk usually occur on the announced day once weather and mitigation windows are locked. The two prior slips (20 November to 23 November, then to 25 November) were voluntary adjustments for exactly those factors; no further postponement has been announced as of 23 November, and the court has not enjoined the emergency-exemption path the Justice Department has already asserted.

The residual risk is a rapid additional court order specifically blocking even the exemption, or a same-day weather or operational abort. Neither has materialized, and further delay would itself increase the temperature-driven hazard the Army says it is trying to avoid.

an uncontrolled blast as temperatures drop.
* **2026-11-22 (Direction: Toward YES on Nov 25 specifically):** The Army bypassed the Monday/Tuesday window and officially rescheduled the detonation to Wednesday, Nov 25, 2026, citing more optimal weather conditions and time to emplace mitigation measures.
* **2026-11-23 (Direction: Strongly Toward NO):** On Monday afternoon, President Donald Trump intervened directly via Truth Social, announcing that he was overruling the Army's plan to bypass the court. Trump stated he "ordered the Military not to do so until such time as the Eighth Circuit agrees that we can go forward, and am further making this decision fully subject to the incoming Governor Elect, Rob Sand, agreeing to the operation". Incoming Democratic Governor-elect Rob Sand has been sharply critical of the Army's lack of transparency and public notice regarding the detonation.

Because the Commander-in-Chief has explicitly ordered the military to stand down until *both* the Eighth Circuit lifts its administrative stay *and* Governor-elect Rob Sand explicitly gives his agreement, the hurdles to carrying out the detonation within the next 48 hours (on Wednesday, Nov 25) are formidable.

### (3) Strongest Reason the Obvious Outcome Might Fail
The obvious outcome now is that the detonation is halted and does not occur on November 25. However, this could fail (resulting in a YES resolution) because President Trump coupled his veto condition with an explicit political ultimatum: he declared that if the materials spontaneously explode, he will hold Governor-elect Rob Sand personally responsible for "any and all death or destruction caused by this very unfortunate, and longterm, situation," while noting that current weather on Wednesday is optimal. Faced with this intense political and safety pressure, and given that the DOJ already urged the Eighth Circuit on Nov 22 to lift the stay immediately due to the imminent cold-weather threat, it remains possible that the Eighth Circuit dissolves its administrative stay on Tuesday, Nov 24, and Rob Sand reluctantly consents to avoid bearing sole blame for a potential catastrophic accident, clearing the Army to execute the blast on its already-prepared Wednesday, Nov 25 schedule.

Balancing the direct presidential stand-down order and dual-approval requirement against the urgent safety pressure that could force a rapid resolution on Tuesday, I estimate a 15% chance the detonation proceeds on Wednesday, November 25.

facts.fact: Acting Army Secretary Adam Telle postponed the planned November 20 controlled detonation of degraded lead azide at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant to Monday, November 23.

The U.S. Court of Appeals for the Eighth Circuit granted an administrative stay suspending the EPA's emergency permit for the lead azide detonation following a lawsuit by the Iowa Environmental Council and Sierra Club.

The Department of Justice filed a notice with the Eighth Circuit stating that the Army intended to invoke an emergency exemption under the Resource Conservation and Recovery Act to carry out the controlled detonation without the stayed EPA permit.

On November 22, the U.S. Army rescheduled the controlled detonation at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant to Wednesday, November 25, citing more optimal weather conditions and time to emplace mitigation measures.

President Donald Trump announced on Monday that he ordered the military not to proceed with the Wednesday detonation until the Eighth Circuit approves the operation and Iowa Governor-elect Rob Sand agrees to it.
Iowa Governor-elect Rob Sand stated on Sunday that because of past decisions no good options exist, the situation is dangerous and unpredictable, and Iowans deserve transparency and accountability.
